solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In well-known tragedy, mischief left one in Jock's possession

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside what the Scotsman holds, so the word in marks an insertion

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman; his possession is taken as the swagger of the tough guy
the Roman numeral for one
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A famous tragedy where somebody leaves something with a Scotsman to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: MALICHO comes from Hamlet's 'miching mallecho', so the well-known tragedy is Hamlet; L and I go inside MACHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet uses the obscure word for skulking wickedness, so it means mischief only within that play's language.

clue.text: Hearts, the ones for taming Tweedsmuir Scotsmen

indicators.note: the ones points back to Hearts, so we take the central letters of each following word

parts.note: the two central letters of a six-letter word
the two central letters of a ten-letter word
the two central letters of an eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Scotsmen from Tweedsmuir with brave hearts setting out to tame something wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts does double duty: it defines the answer and tells you to take the middle of each of the three words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A midst is the middle or central part of something, just as the heart is the core of a thing.

clue.text: Bouncer's close before ejecting one in circle

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the word for circle, so in marks the insertion

parts.note: a loop is a ring or circle

indicators.note: ejecting means throwing something out, so a letter is removed from the word for close

parts.note: nigh means near, close at hand
the Roman numeral for one, the letter thrown out

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman at closing time throwing someone out of a circle of drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface bouncer is a doorman, but here it is the cricket kind. A long hop is a short-pitched delivery in cricket that bounces up invitingly to be hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are short-pitched cricket deliveries that rise off the pitch, so a long hop is loosely a type of bouncing ball.

clue.text: Church play area unwilling to display historical shroud material

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rec is a recreation ground
loth is a spelling of loath, meaning reluctant

explanation.surface: A church refusing to put a historical shroud on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerecloth was waxed cloth formerly used to wrap the dead, so it is old-fashioned burial fabric.

clue.text: In other words, Gray depicts a revel

indicators.note: read as de-picts, it means take away the painter, an artist being someone who depicts

parts.note: or introduces a rewording, as in 'the doctor, or physician'
taken as written before the painter is removed

explanation.surface: A comment on a poem or painting by Gray that shows a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword painter; 'de-pict' him out of GRAY and GY remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild party of excessive indulgence, a riotous celebration.

clue.text: Refer to what I said months back about transmitted ideas

indicators.note: going back means the assembled letters are read from right to left

parts.note: to cite is to refer to, and me stands for the speaker
m is an abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Someone asking to be quoted from a speech made months ago about spreading ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Memetic means relating to memes, units of culture copied and passed between people.

clue.text: Futurist Communist leader restricting chatter against outer space

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so one word encloses another

parts.note: Mao Zedong led Communist China
to yak is to chatter
v for versus
the sky is the heavens above

explanation.surface: A Communist leader silencing chatter that opposes space exploration.
explanation.walkthrough: Futurist has a capital because it names the early twentieth-century art movement, not a forecaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Mayakovsky was the leading Russian poet of the Futurist movement.

clue.text: Raising this liquor made from flowers is a big hit

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wham is a heavy blow

explanation.surface: A flower liquor that becomes a big success once it is launched.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: turn the answer up and you get the big hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahwa is an Indian tree whose sweet flowers are fermented and distilled into a strong spirit.

clue.text: From main character's angle, a green soup

parts.note: from someone's point of view is 'to them', so to the hero
taken as written

explanation.surface: A story told from the protagonist's viewpoint, with a bowl of green soup in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Toheroa is a New Zealand shellfish famous for a rich soup that is distinctively green.

clue.text: American native strips in California

indicators.note: the cartoons sit inside the state abbreviation, so in marks an insertion

parts.note: Cal is a short form of California
comix is a spelling of comics, i.e. comic strips

explanation.surface: A Native American undressing somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: American native sounds like a person, but it is an animal native to America: the ringtail, a raccoon relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacomistle or ringtail is a small raccoon-like mammal found in Mexico and the southwestern United States.

clue.text: Study ditch height across odd parts of gully for cutting in wood

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the word for ditch and height enclose the kept letters

parts.note: a den is a private study
to ditch something is to drop it
h is the abbreviation for height

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth, are the letters kept

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word

explanation.surface: Someone surveying a ditch across a gully for a woodcutting job.
explanation.walkthrough: Ditch here is a verb, to abandon, though the surface makes it a trench beside the gully.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendroglyph is a carving made in the bark or trunk of a living tree.

clue.text: For Romans, this is almost Rhenish

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hock is wine from the Rhine region of Germany

explanation.surface: A remark that Roman drinkers found Rhine wine nearly perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhenish means from the Rhine, and hock is the old British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoc is the Latin neuter demonstrative pronoun, so a Roman would write it where we write 'this'.

clue.text: Not clever to smother constant sound of encouragement

indicators.note: to smother is to cover over completely, so one word engulfs another

parts.note: thick means stupid
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: An observation that smothering someone with constant praise is a foolish way to encourage them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tchick is the clicking noise made with the tongue to urge on a horse.

clue.text: To grasp location of grand mausoleum, cursorily study photo of shadows

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it inside, so one word encloses another

parts.note: to skim is to read quickly and superficially
Agra in India is the home of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A tourist glancing at a guide to find where a great tomb is.
explanation.walkthrough: The grand mausoleum is the Taj Mahal, which stands in the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiagram is an X-ray image or shadowgraph, recorded by shadows cast on a plate.

clue.text: Sprite before tea drunk by Parisian's the French one

indicators.note: something drunk by a person goes inside them, so these letters are placed within others

parts.note: le is the French masculine article
pre is a prefix meaning before
cha is slang for tea
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink served before tea to a Parisian.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprite looks like the brand of lemonade, sitting nicely with tea and drinking; it is a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is a mischievous little fairy of Irish folklore.

clue.text: In lead, recovers alchemised gold, by reports

indicators.note: the transformed letters go inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: alchemy transmutes one substance into another, so these letters are transformed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearrangement
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
x as in a 3 x 4 grid, read as by

explanation.surface: An alchemist turning lead into gold, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the alchemist's dream of turning lead into gold, and both metals appear as chemical symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Proces-verbaux are official written records or minutes of proceedings, a French legal term.

clue.text: Reverse picture of dress trim in Covent Garden venue

indicators.note: the earlier words go inside the venue's abbreviation, so in marks an insertion

parts.note: the Royal Opera House stands in Covent Garden
to tog is to dress
an old sense of trim is to rebuke or scold, which is to rap

explanation.surface: A back view of a costume's trimmings in the Royal Opera House.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse looks like a turnaround signal, but it belongs to the definition: the picture is a negative image.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotograph is a photographic copy, usually of a manuscript, printed white on black, the tones reversed.

clue.text: A half-hearted religious founder born originally in sheikhdom

indicators.note: with only half its heart, the founder's name loses one of its two central letters

parts.note: taken as written
the founder of Buddhism
b is the abbreviation for born

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the first letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lukewarm religious leader who was born in a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven emirates of the UAE, ruled by a sheikh.

clue.text: Gasbags for some British planes carrying sweats

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside, so one set of letters goes within another

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for British
a horse in a lather is sweating heavily
kite is old slang for an aeroplane

explanation.surface: British planes carrying sportswear, gasbags being balloons or airships.
explanation.walkthrough: The British planes are B KITES, split open to carry the sweats. Gasbags suggests airships alongside the planes, but it means talkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherskite is someone who talks at length about nothing, a windbag, a word chiefly Scottish and American.

clue.text: One-eyed northerner with snake touring border area

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so the snake surrounds the other letters

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
a rim is an edge
a is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A Cyclops-like figure from the north travelling with a snake around a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arimaspians were a legendary people of the far north in Herodotus, said to have a single eye each.

clue.text: Ben's name comes up, admitting personnel confessed

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so other letters are placed inside
in a down clue coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Scotland
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A man called Ben being named at work and owning up to staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben is a Scottish word for mountain; the best-known one's name is Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shriven is to have made confession to a priest and received absolution.

clue.text: Private broadcast over meeting points on head

parts.note: Pte is the abbreviation for the army rank of private

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A private soldier's broadcast about reaching meeting points ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Each pterion is a spot on the side of the skull where four bones join together.

clue.text: Developed cities, DC for example, here and now

indicators.note: land that has been developed is rebuilt into a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearrangement
taken as written for rearrangement

explanation.surface: Developed cities like Washington DC as places of the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Deictic words such as here, now, this and that point to context and take meaning from the speaker's situation.

clue.text: Sri Lankan monkey said to pull on grass

indicators.note: said means spoken, so it is the sound of the words that matters

parts.note: a toke is a drag on a cannabis joint, grass being slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A monkey in Sri Lanka reportedly tugging at the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull on grass suggests a monkey tugging at turf, but grass is cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: The toque macaque is a monkey native to Sri Lanka, named for its cap-like tuft of hair.

clue.text: I try to spoil Filipino miner

parts.note: taken as written
to have a go is to try
to rot is to decay or spoil

explanation.surface: A Filipino miner admitting he tries to cause damage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Igorot are mountain peoples of northern Luzon, long known for gold and copper mining.

clue.text: Rocket man regularly inspected amount of obscured sky

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: letters two, four, six and eight of the phrase

explanation.surface: An astronaut regularly checking how cloudy the sky is.
explanation.definitionFit: An okta is the meteorological unit of cloud cover: one eighth of the sky hidden by cloud.

clue.text: Polynesian drink: in local dress you'll want large one double

indicators.note: to want is to lack, so the letter for large is left out
only one of a doubled pair is wanted, so a repeated half is dropped

parts.note: the lava-lava is the wraparound skirt worn in Polynesia
l is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A dress code note: wear the local costume, and order a large drink, a double.
explanation.walkthrough: The lava-lava is a doubled word; keep one half, LAVA, and lose the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava is another name for kava, the ceremonial Polynesian drink made from a pepper plant's root.

clue.text: Once I faked noise from bird tray

definitions.note: a first-person description of the impostor stands for the noun: one who faked

parts.note: the call of a duck
a salver is a serving tray

explanation.surface: A confession: I once faked the sound of a bird from behind a tray.
explanation.walkthrough: Once marks the word as archaic, and 'I faked' is the impostor speaking of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A quacksalver is an old word for a charlatan who peddled fake remedies, a quack doctor.

clue.text: Poet's to make productive politician prevail, putting the writer first

indicators.note: the self-reference letter is taken out of its place and set at the front instead

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as I
a Member of Parliament
to reign is to prevail or hold sway

explanation.surface: A poet's urging that a politician should win through by thinking of the writer first.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the I already sitting in the word for prevail; it is moved to the front rather than added.
explanation.definitionFit: Impregn is a poetic form of impregnate, used by Milton, meaning to make fertile.

clue.text: Send cuckoo with both wings replaced by a diving bird

indicators.text: with both wings replaced by a
indicators.note: wings are the outermost letters, and each is swapped for the letter named

parts.note: to unhinge someone is to drive them mad

explanation.surface: Sending a cuckoo off after its wings are swapped for a bird that dives.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like a bird to match the diving bird, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The anhinga or snakebird is an American water bird that swims underwater to spear fish.
